title: BigQuery measures is now GA: Unifying BI metrics and knowledge graphs for AI accuracy
summary: To answer a complex business question, an AI agent must understand two things: what happened, and why. The what is a governed metric, like revenue at risk; the why is the network of relationships that produced it. Because metric definitions, a.k.a. measures, traditionally live in business intelligence (BI) platforms while relationships live in knowledge graphs, an AI agent only ever sees half the picture. It guesses the rest, leading to confident but sometimes wrong answers. To solve this hallucination problem, we introduced measures in BigQuery, which are now generally available. Historically, organizations needing both BI and knowledge graphs had to run two siloed technology stacks: one to calculate reliable metrics, the other to map out entity relationships. Bridging them entailed brittle data pipelines and runtime reconciliation by analysts and AI agents, who held the connections in their heads or in sprawling prompts. This patchwork approach wasn't just slow and expensive — it’s where data governance broke down, as every analyst and prompt may define joins and metrics differently. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! And, of course, you buy what will be useful for that most wonderful of pursuits, blind research, which is research without direction for the sheer joy of it.
